intro: You are going to read about an old man who lives with a small robot helper.

passage: Park Min-ho is 81 years old. He lives alone in a small flat in Busan, a city by the sea in South Korea. His wife died four years ago, and his children live in Seoul, five hours away by car. "After my wife died, the flat was very quiet," he says. "I was lonely. Some days I didn't speak to anybody."

Last spring, his granddaughter Ji-woo gave him a present: a small white robot. It is about the size of a cat, it has a round screen for a face, and it can move around the flat on wheels. Mr Park was not happy at first. "I said, 'I don't need a toy. I'm not a child!'" he remembers.

But the robot is not a toy. It is a clever device that helps him every day. In the morning, it says "Good morning!" and tells him about the weather. It reminds him to take his medicine at nine o'clock and at six o'clock. It can also connect him with his family. When he says, "Call Ji-woo," her face appears on the screen and they can talk.

The robot has a friendly voice, and Mr Park has given it a name: Dori. Every evening, Dori asks him questions about his day and records his answers. If he doesn't answer for a long time, the robot sends a message to his son. "Once, I fell in the kitchen," Mr Park says. "Dori called my son, and he called an ambulance. That was very useful!"

Of course, Dori is not perfect. Sometimes it doesn't understand Mr Park's words, and he must charge its battery every night. Some people think that robots can never take the place of real people, and Mr Park agrees. "My family is more important," he says. "But Dori is a great invention. Now my flat isn't so quiet, and I'm never really alone."
